every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: Paltusotine, a quinoline-containing basic amine structurally related to the query's quinoline/quinuclidine scaffold, had a human absolute oral bioavailability of 69% (90% CI 59-82%) after a 20 mg oral solution versus IV microtracer.

Moxifloxacin, a methoxy-substituted quinolone bearing a basic bicyclic amine, had human absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 82-92% across studies, including 91% for a 400-mg tablet under fasting conditions.

All numeric F values in the visible L1 records are at or above 37%, and none indicate F below the 20% threshold; additional human absolute-bioavailability values include prasugrel ~79%, GSK1322322 77% fed, veralipride 78.6%, and apixaban 37-39% with rifampin.

The query's physicochemical profile (MW 324, logD 1.29, TPSA 45.6, HBD 1, no Lipinski violations) is consistent with the high-F comparators, and the low neutral fraction is not disqualifying given the ionizable basic amines in paltusotine and moxifloxacin.

evidence_gaps: No direct human absolute oral bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule.
No experimental permeability, solubility, or first-pass metabolism data are available for the query.

Transfer from paltusotine and moxifloxacin is based on structural analogy rather than an exact match; the query contains a quinuclidine tertiary amine and a vinyl group not present in those comparators.
Some supporting records are predicted human values or were measured under special conditions (e.g., rifampin induction), limiting direct transferability.
No formulation or food-effect data are available for the query.
